title: Uzziah
lead: King of Judah in the 700s BC, called Azariah in most of Kings and Uzziah elsewhere. His long, prosperous reign ended in a skin disease that Chronicles explains by his attempt to burn incense in the temple. Isaiah saw his vision in the year Uzziah died.

sections.b: Kings tells his reign briefly as Azariah's: fifty-two years, a good king who left the high places, struck with skin disease and confined to a separate house while his son Jotham governed (2 Kings 14:21–22; 2 Kings 15:1–7). Chronicles adds his wars, building, farms and army, and the story of his pride in the temple (2 Chronicles 26). The prophets date their work by him (Isaiah 1:1; Hosea 1:1; Amos 1:1), and Isaiah's call comes "in the year King Uzziah died" (Isaiah 6:1). An earthquake in his days was remembered centuries later (Amos 1:1; Zechariah 14:5). Matthew lists him among Jesus' ancestors (Matthew 1:8–9).
